text.p: ORLANDO, Jan 24, Reuter - Brunswick Corp is shopping for non-boating acquisitions with the view of moving away from reliance on the cyclical marine businesses by the turn of the century, chief fiancial officer Peter Hamilton said on Friday.

Even with recent acquisitions, Hamiton told an investors conference sponsored by AG Edwards & Sons Inc that about 65 percent of Brunswick revenues come from making outboard motors, boats and marine accessories. The company wants at least half of the revenues, estimated by AG Edwards analyst Tim Conder to have been $3.12 billion last year, to come from other active-sporting businesses.
"We think we can get that done in the next couple of years," Hamilton said.

Well-known for its bowling alleys and equipment, Lake Forest, Illinois-based Brunswick last year paid $154 million for Igloo Holdings Inc, a maker of ice chests, and $120 million for tent-maker American Camper. It also bought the Roadmaster Bicycle business for $212 million.

"We are developing as an active-recreation company with a big marine products arm," Hamilton said. He said Wall Street would award Brunswick a higher value if it was less reliant on marine businesses, widely regarded as highly cyclical.
Hamilton said Brunswick was interested in buying companies in outdoor recreation segments, since it can use databases on existing customers to spur sales in the new areas.
"What we are really trying to do, and mainly through acquisitions, is sell more products to more people," he said.
